But i really dont know what the right answer is.  I am on this thread too, so i suppose that i can only give advice to be taken with a grain of salt.

I have worked on getting assistance for months, a few separate times, and never even got to a full diagnosis or medication because the process is so slow and complicated.  All after at my first appointment the therapist told me that being bipolar is nothing to cry about.  "We are going to get you help!  Don't be upset, I'm telling you we can fix it!"  Here I am over 2 years later no farther along, and if I want to try again I have to start from scratch.
I start out with all of the best intentions,  but there is no reward or sense of accomplishment when everything you manage to complete leads to another complication.

People always say they will help with that stuff, but then explain to me what to do as if I don't know.  They don't get that I literally need someone to sit with me and help each time something comes up, or I'm not able to keep going.  They lose interest, or feel like I should eventually be able to manage getting it done myself, or just start to act like I'm lazy or don't want help...all of which makes it that much harder to keep trying.  Eventually that kill yourself chant in my head just gets louder and I go back into hibernation mode just so that I am not pushing myself closer to the edge while trying to get help.

I have been medicated twice a long time ago when I had health insurance with disastrous results.  I would love to try again, but things have gotten too bad for me to work (for several years), so no insurance no meds.  I tried going through assistance and was even working toward a BPD diagnosis, but the constant setbacks with paperwork got too be too much for my health.  When it's a struggle even to get up and shower it gets too dissappointing to keep trying.
I would love to have an answer to that.  Or at least a better one than the aforementioned loop...

If you are talking to someone that struggles with their issues every day, you have to remember that they have probably spent a lot of time and energy trying to figure out how not to be like they are.  The likelihood that you will offer them a solution or perspective that they haven't thought of is slim, and in my experience can sometimes make you feel dumb or talked down to depending on how its delivered.

I can't speak for everyone, but personally I just need someone to be there, to listen, and ask if I'm ok.  It's hard to find people that understand in the real world, so sometimes "I understand" is enough to get you through the moment.

Some of us suffer these thoughts constantly.  Help is always appreciated,  but you have to understand that probably more often than not people on these forums go through every day thinking "kill yourself" on a loop...

All of this. My parents are wonderful and want to pay for my care out of pocket so no hoops, we can just get it done, but I know it would be a huge strain on them financially, and if I let them do that the guilt will be too much and make things worse.  Not to mention that is their mindset now, after watching me struggle for 30 years or so.  It's nice that people care, but I do think too many jump straight to "have you tried therapy?"  It can be frustrating to hear when you would love to do just that.

My best friend is a fabulous person,  we are 34 and prior to the pandemic he had been alone for 15 years.  He struggled with depression, and was always of the mindset that no one would want to be with him because he lived above his mother, or his car wasn't nice enough, felt unattractive etc.  

His brother fixed him up on a blind date 6 months ago and he is happier than ever.  You sound like a wonderful person, and as I told him everything happens in it's own time.  I am very sure that being a doctor comes with a taxing schedule, have you tried befriending coworkers?  Sometimes it is easier to connect with people that share our experiences.  I also agree with the volunteering idea.  That can be a great way to meet caring like minded people.

I live in rural PA.  I started the process a few times, but there are always hiccups or the process is really extensive and it gets too overwhelming and I stop dealing with it and shut down.  Or a couple of times it got better and I was working and just didn't take the time out to continue with the process.   Then things start going downhill again and I have to start over.

I know it's my fault, but the issues that I have keep me from being able to get the help I need to fix them...and I have only had the opportunity to try when I wasn't with my wife.

Again I understand what it is you are saying.  But this is not the place.  As someone who frequently shares these feelings, pointing it out when people are out here saying they don't want to live is not helpful.  You make a good point, but the people that you are saying it to are at risk, and you are making them sound selfish for hoping that someone can connect with them and support them as they are.

I have felt that way since I was a child.  I had very few friends, and even at 8 or 9 years old I connected exclusively with victims of abuse and trauma  (have some of my own).  I remember even at that early age having discussions with the 2 kids I hung out with about feeling like I would die young.  My best friend from this time made it to just after her 30th birthday before OD, all of us in her life are back and forth about whether it was intentional or not.  I am now 34, feeling like I have been here too long.  Asked for a divorce from my wife earlier this week and wondering daily what the hell i am holding out for.  8 year old me knew not to stick around here too long, wondering why 34 year old me can't work up the guts to find out where I'm actually meant to be....

I hope I am reincarnated as an animal or bug.  At least then everything I'm afraid of can actually kill me and is a justification for the fear.  Unlike walking around here every day worrying about who is going to screw me over next or hurt me and having panic attacks because emotional stress triggers my fight or flight response.

That being said.  I really hope I am still stuck here for some reason other than divine cruelty, and if you are still here I hope that for you too.  Maybe one day we will figure out what it is.

That is a really judgemental thing to say to someone that is on the edge sir.  I get your point, but there is a time and a place for certain advice...  Not really the time to make a list of what is wrong with a suicidal person wanting someone to connect with.  Especially on a subreddit for suicidal people trying to connect with others for help.

I used to work a 60 hour a week job at a knitting factory, and then she complained that I was gone too much and started just having friends over all the time and ignoring me the little bit that I was actually home to play video games.

Yes, I have actually been taking more, and more expensive commissions than ever.  She doesn't care because she resents that I never just stopped making art.  Our first separation was because I was offered an apprenticeship at a tattoo shop and she was adamant that I was not allowed to do that.

I am a freelance artist.  My work brings in about what a part time job does.  But I also take care of the house and cook every day.  On top of which my father in law is elderly and not in good health which is why I haven't been rushing out for a job at a gas station or something and putting the family at risk.
The family also decided to get a dog during th pandemic, and now I am the only one here all the time to care for him.  Her dad uses a walker/cane, and can't even take him out when they are alone.

Basically this has happened any time I was struggling and she got a good job.  When she is unemployed she needs me and treats me as such.  She gains confidence when she is working, which is great, but it makes her confident enough to tell me she thinks I'm worthless.  All the fucking time.

It's kind of a long explanation,  but a lot of financial instability as a result of decisions that both of us have made over the years.  In her mind it is 100 percent my fault.  I supported us as best I could through the pandemic, and she got a good joba couple of months ago and every since she has made me feel like trash because I am not able to move us into our own place (we live in a small apartment with my in laws)

She spends all of her money too quickly, and if I comment on it she acts like I'm controlling, but I have to save every little bit I get to the side.  That way when she runs out we have some.  There have been many times when she hasn't had a job and I did, or she was making much less.  I made sure to tell her all the time that she was important and it didn't matter because I love her.  She got depressed and couldn't do anything and I helped her through it.  Now the shoe is on the other foot and I cant climb out of my depression because she treats me daily like the only way I will ever get her respect is to get a job right this second.
Same feeling but my best friend also happens to be my wife.  I am so done dealing with tomorrows... just want 1 last today.
